page: Hetzner Cloud cpx31 is a virtual instance built on the x86_64 architecture and provisioned via the QEMU hypervisor. The configuration features 4 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz, backed by 16 MB of L3 cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1 data cache. The instance includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing roughly 1.95 GB of RAM per vCPU, along with 160 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. It operates without integrated hardware accelerators and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance profiles demonstrate competent compute capabilities paired with moderate memory throughput. Single-core stress-ng tests position the processor in the top 25%, while Geekbench scores reach 1463 for single-core and 4741 for multi-core evaluations. Memory subsystem evaluations reveal 60.53 GB/sec uncached large-block read throughput and 41.8 GB/sec write throughput, placing overall PassMark memory performance in the bottom 25%. Instruction support includes AVX, AES, and SHA_NI, though AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent. Workloads with heavy memory intensity or parallel build tasks, such as Clang compilation and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, fall into lower performance percentiles.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio delivers compute density at an economical tier, making cpx31 cost-effective for general compute tasks that do not exceed the 8.0 GB memory envelope. However, the shared core allocation poses tradeoffs for sustained multithreaded operations subject to noisy neighbor constraints. The bundled 160 GB NVMe storage provides strong local disk speed without external block storage costs. The instance is suited for lightweight web applications, staging environments, small container clusters, API gateways, and non-memory-intensive batch processing.
description: Hetzner Cloud cpx31 is an x86_64 cloud server provisioned via QEMU, featuring 4 shared vCPUs on an AMD EPYC processor at 2.0 GHz, 8.0 GB of system memory, and 160 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. Operating with a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and lacking dedicated GPU accelerators, it targets compute workloads requiring moderate memory. In benchmarks, the cpx31 exhibits strong single-core compute performance in stress-ng evaluations, while Geekbench multi-core and memory throughput reflect average-to-conservative tiers. PassMark memory testing and multi-threaded decompression highlight throughput constraints under data-intensive pressure. With its shared CPU model, cpx31 provides an economical compute profile for general-purpose application hosting, development environments, background job processing, and lightweight microservices that fit inside an 8.0 GB operating memory boundary.
